Installing package wp-cli/profile-command (this may take a while)...
Updating package index...
Success: Package installed.
commands.tip: wp profile is not bundled with WP-CLI core — install it once per environment before using any subcommand below.
Run this first on any "site feels slow" ticket. On multisite, always pass --url — without it you profile the network's main site, not the one anyone complained about.
template is the slow stage here — 0.2890s with a cache_ratio of only 61.4%. Next: isolate it to see how much is hook_time.
73.7% of bootstrap is hook_time — active plugins doing work on plugins_loaded/init. Fast enough here, but the column to watch on a slower site.
Almost no hook_time — a simple pre_get_posts with no extra meta_query/tax_query stacked on top.
86.9% of this stage is hook_time — this isn't a slow theme file, it's whatever is hooked onto the render. Next: wp profile hook on the specific hook.
This is how you go from "template is slow" to a named function: crm_widget_track_pageview alone accounts for most of the stage's time.
Benchmarks a raw PHP snippet without a full request — useful for isolating one function call before it ever gets hooked into a page.
Same as wp profile eval, reading the snippet from a file — easier to keep and reuse than retyping it in the terminal.

commands.output:
usage: wp profile stage [<stage>] [--url=<url>] [--fields=<fields>] [--format=<format>]
   or: wp profile hook [<hook>] [--url=<url>]
   or: wp profile eval <php-code>
   or: wp profile eval-file <file>
commands.tip: Four subcommands total. stage and hook are for a real request; eval and eval-file are for testing a snippet in isolation.

commands.output:
Profiling commands measure how long each stage of a WordPress request takes, and how much of that time is hooked plugin/theme code.

Available commands:
• wp package install wp-cli/profile-command  - Install the profiling package
• wp profile stage                           - Profile bootstrap, main_query, template
• wp profile stage <stage>                   - Isolate one stage, see hook_time
• wp profile hook <hook>                     - Profile callbacks on one hook
• wp profile eval <code>                     - Benchmark a raw PHP snippet
• wp profile eval-file <file>                - Benchmark PHP from a file

Anchors:
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/profiling/#wp-profile-stage
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/profiling/#wp-profile-stage-stage
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/profiling/#wp-profile-hook
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/profiling/#notes-on-reading-wp-profile-output
commands.tip: wp profile stage → isolate the slow stage → wp profile hook. Three commands cover most "site is slow" tickets.
